anchors.paper_title: MEG-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extended to magnetoencephalography
anchors.reason: MEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard specification used to format this dataset, not a paper describing the MEG-SCANS recordings.

metadata.methods_description: MEG was recorded from 24 participants during auditory listening to audiobooks, OLSA matrix sentences at intelligibility levels from 20% to 95%, and up-chirps. Auxiliary channels captured the left and right audio signals and the instructor's microphone at 1000 Hz. Pre- and post-session empty-room recordings, structural MRI, and behavioral audiogram and SRT hearing screenings were also collected. Raw data were additionally MaxFiltered.

citation_details.title: Brain-to-Language Decoding: Paradigms, Signals, Methods, Evaluation, Practical Use and Beyond
citation_details.author: Yiqian Yang, Yiqun Duan, Chenyu Liu, Yiqi Wang, Xinliang Zhou, Chin-Teng Lin, Yu Zhang
citation_details.abstract: Brain-to-language decoding translates neural activity associated with language production, internal speech and perception into linguistic or expressive outputs. It offers a route to restoring communication after speech loss and a means of studying how the brain represents language. Advances in neural recording and representation learning have expanded the field from constrained recognition and acoustic reconstruction to text generation, streaming personalised speech and facial animation. This survey synthesises these developments across invasive and non-invasive measurements. We connect Articulated, Inner and Perceived paradigms to the neural populations they engage, the representations available to decoders and the outputs those representations can support. We examine model development, public resources and the evolution of evaluation, and compare published performance and communication costs within their reported protocols. citation_details.title: Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference
citation_details.author: Boumediene Hamzi, Houman Owhadi
citation_details.abstract: When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph. We extend the characterization to nonzero means and show that freely varying correlated noise forces a fixed linear log-odds decoder to retain the full quadratic feature span even for two distinct centered regimes. citation_details.title: An EEG dataset for structured auditory sequence processing with Morse code sounds
citation_details.author: Zhongyang He, Ying Zeng, Siyuan Zhang, Changfu Pei, Li Tong, Kunlin Guo, Yuanlong Gao, Bao Li, Bin Yan
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Auditory processing of structured sound sequences requires information to be integrated across time while preserving sequence content and order, allowing different properties of the same auditory input to guide different behavioral decisions. Yet openly available human EEG resources remain limited for studying explicitly structured auditory sequences processed under different decision rules within the same participants. Here we present MorseEEG-ATP, a two-task EEG dataset from 32 Morse-naïve adults who listened to the same set of 78 single-character Morse-code sounds while performing dot-count and first–last matching tasks. The dataset combines shared auditory input with distinct decision rules, enabling investigation of sequence-level temporal and structural variation, task-associated EEG and behavioral features, and cross-task correspondence and generalization. citation_details.author: Li Guo, Yang Li, Junli Wang, Yuqi Feng, Baojun Wu, Yinglong Xu
citation_details.abstract: Objective electrophysiological markers are often proposed for speech-in-noise assessment, but their validation targets are not always explicit: a marker may calibrate with intelligibility, distinguish acoustic conditions, decode attention, or predict an individual speech reception threshold (SRT). We used three public MEG/EEG datasets to test these endpoints within one validation framework. In MEG-SCANS (22 normal-hearing listeners), delta-band sentence-level envelope reconstruction increased with target intelligibility (Friedman chi-square=31.27, p = 8.3e-6). citation_details.title: Analysis of the influence of gradual changes in matrix sentence similarity on neural envelope tracking
citation_details.author: Till Habersetzer, Bernd T. Meyer, Andreas Radeloff
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Neural tracking of speech is a well-established phenomenon in neuroscience. However, for speech signals with a fixed structure, significant correlations between speech envelopes and neurophysiological representations occur even for unheard sentences. We exploit a structured speech-in-noise matrix hearing test (Oldenburger Sentence Test, OLSA) to systematically quantify the relationship between acoustic sentence similarity and neural tracking. Simultaneous magnetoencephalography (MEG) and 76-channel electroencephalography (EEG) data, including 16 channels positioned directly around the ears (ear-EEG), were recorded from 21 young adults with normal hearing during the presentation of clean-speech audiobooks and OLSA sentences at six signal-to-noise ratios. citation_details.title: MIRA-Net: A Cross-Cohort Representation Learning Framework for Parkinson’s Disease Classification Using Acoustic and Beta-Band MEG Biomarkers
citation_details.author: N Akhila, Asif Ekbal, D. Pomeroy
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Accurate diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease (PD) remains challenging due to substantial inter-subject variability and the absence of widely accessible, objective multimodal biomarkers. Although speech and magnetoencephalography (MEG) biomarkers have individually demonstrated strong discriminative potential, their joint utilization is constrained by the absence of subject-level paired datasets—a fundamental gap that has prevented cross-modal validation at the individual level. We argue that this makes cross-cohort representation learning not merely a pragmatic workaround, but the most realistic and clinically transferable framework for multimodal PD assessment. In real-world deployment, acoustic screening and neuroimaging biomarkers are acquired through separate clinical pathways and must be integrated across heterogeneous patient populations.
